result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — Spatial Regression and Reporting" subtitle: "Residual autocorrelation · LM tests · spatial lag and error models · impacts · reporting · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 3–4: the outcome is spatially clustered, and we know where - Today: **regression on areas**. The usual assumption of **independent residuals** often fails - By the end you can: - test regression **residuals** for spatial autocorrelation - use **Lagrange multiplier tests** to choose lag or error - fit and compare **spatial lag** and **spatial error** models - **report** a spatial analysis ::: # Topic 1 — Check the residuals {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Fit OLS first ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ols <- lm(dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks) round(summary(ols)$coefficients, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) -101.067 61.802 -1.635 0.106 poverty_index 1.445 0.335 4.306 0.000 literacy_pct 0.981 0.603 1.629 0.107 ``` ::: ::: ## Moran's I on the residuals ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lm.morantest(ols, lw, zero.policy = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Global Moran I for regression residuals data: model: lm(formula = dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks) weights: lw Moran I statistic standard deviate = 4.4335, p-value = 4.635e-06 alternative hypothesis: greater sample estimates: Observed Moran I Expectation Variance 0.273945405 -0.023128244 0.004489825 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} A significant **positive** residual Moran's I means the model leaves spatial structure unexplained: **independence fails** and standard errors are probably **too small**. ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} blocks$res_ols <- residuals(ols) ggplot(blocks) + geom_sf(aes(fill = res_ols)) + scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", name = "Residual") + labs(title = "OLS residuals: neighbours share the same sign") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s5_spatial_regression_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: # Topic 2 — Which spatial model? {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Two structures | Model | Idea | Think of | |---|---|---| | **Spatial lag (SAR)** | my outcome depends on my **neighbours' outcomes** | contagion, spillover | | **Spatial error (SEM)** | **omitted shared factors** make neighbouring errors alike | unmeasured exposures | ::: {.eq} Lag: y = ρWy + Xβ + ε   |   Error: y = Xβ + u, u = λWu + ε ::: ## Lagrange multiplier tests ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} lm.RStests(ols, lw, test = c("RSerr", "RSlag", "adjRSerr", "adjRSlag"), zero.policy = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rao's score (a.k.a Lagrange multiplier) diagnostics for spatial dependence data: model: lm(formula = dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks) test weights: lw RSerr = 14.895, df = 1, p-value = 0.0001137 Rao's score (a.k.a Lagrange multiplier) diagnostics for spatial dependence data: model: lm(formula = dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks) test weights: lw RSlag = 19.289, df = 1, p-value = 1.124e-05 Rao's score (a.k.a Lagrange multiplier) diagnostics for spatial dependence data: model: lm(formula = dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks) test weights: lw adjRSerr = 0.15191, df = 1, p-value = 0.6967 Rao's score (a.k.a Lagrange multiplier) diagnostics for spatial dependence data: model: lm(formula = dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks) test weights: lw adjRSlag = 4.5459, df = 1, p-value = 0.033 ``` ::: ::: ## Choosing from the LM tests ::: {.incremental} - If **only one** plain test is significant, use that model - If **both** are, prefer the model whose **robust** test (`adjRSerr` or `adjRSlag`) is larger and significant - Use **theory** too: contagion points to lag, omitted exposures to error ::: ## Fit and compare ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sem <- errorsarlm(dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks, listw = lw, zero.policy = TRUE) sar <- lagsarlm(dengue_per_100k ~ poverty_index + literacy_pct, data = blocks, listw = lw, zero.policy = TRUE) c(lambda = sem$lambda, rho = sar$rho) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` lambda.lambda rho.rho 0.535 0.515 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} AIC(ols, sem, sar) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` df AIC ols 4 698.4286 sem 5 687.2759 sar 5 684.6838 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(OLS = unname(moran.test(residuals(ols), lw, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate[1]), SEM = unname(moran.test(residuals(sem), lw, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate[1])) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` OLS SEM 0.274 -0.042 ``` ::: ::: Lower AIC is better (same data). The residual Moran's I should fall towards 0. # Topic 3 — Interpreting and reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Coefficients in the lag model {.smaller} ::: {.warn} In a **lag** model a change in one block's poverty also changes its neighbours' rates, which feed back. The coefficient is **not** the whole effect. Report **impacts**: direct, indirect and total. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(6) summary(impacts(sar, listw = lw, R = 199), zstats = TRUE, short = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Impact measures (lag, exact): Direct Indirect Total poverty_index dy/dx 0.9339023 0.8647157 1.798618 literacy_pct dy/dx 0.8134276 0.7531661 1.566594 ======================================================== Simulation results ( variance matrix): ======================================================== Simulated standard errors Direct Indirect Total poverty_index dy/dx 0.3400153 0.5790857 0.7998079 literacy_pct dy/dx 0.6010227 0.8975023 1.4072140 Simulated z-values: Direct Indirect Total poverty_index dy/dx 2.715598 1.5611009 2.284744 literacy_pct dy/dx 1.332292 0.9089538 1.148742 Simulated p-values: Direct Indirect Total poverty_index dy/dx 0.0066156 0.11850 0.022328 literacy_pct dy/dx 0.1827641 0.36337 0.250662 ``` ::: ::: In the **error** model the coefficients keep the OLS meaning, with corrected standard errors. ## Other routes ::: {.incremental} - **Add covariates** that explain the clustering; the residual autocorrelation may vanish - **Count data with unequal populations**: Poisson models with a spatial random effect (CAR / BYM in `INLA`, `brms`) - **Geographically weighted regression** lets coefficients vary over space - Always **map the residuals** ::: ## Reporting checklist ::: {.good} 1. The **outcome** (rate, not count) and the **areas**, with the **CRS** if distances were used 2. The **weights**: definition, standardisation, isolates 3. **Global** result: Moran's I, p-value type, simulations 4. **Local** results: method, adjustment, map; say they are exploratory 5. **Regression**: residual Moran's I, LM tests, model chosen and why, parameter (`rho` or `lambda`), AIC vs OLS, impacts for a lag model 6. **Limitations**: area size (MAUP), small numbers, edge effects, association not cause ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `gis-workshop/labs/lab5_regression.R` - `lm()` then `lm.morantest()` · map the residuals - `lm.RStests()` · `errorsarlm()` · `lagsarlm()` · `AIC()` - `impacts()` for the lag model ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkkmp0.4t433a" data-show="U3RhbmRhcmQgZXJyb3JzIGFyZSBwcm9iYWJseSB0b28gc21hbGwsIHNvIHAtdmFsdWVzIGFy ZSBvcHRpbWlzdGlj" data-explain="UG9zaXRpdmUgcmVzaWR1YWwgYXV0b2NvcnJlbGF0aW9uIG1lYW5zIG5laWdoYm91cmluZyBy ZXNpZHVhbHMgc2hhcmUgaW5mb3JtYXRpb24sIHNvIHRoZXJlIGFyZSBmZXdlciBpbmRlcGVu ZGVudCBvYnNlcnZhdGlvbnMgdGhhbiB0aGUgbW9kZWwgYXNzdW1lcyBhbmQgc3RhbmRhcmQg ZXJyb3JzIGFyZSB0b28gc21hbGwu"} Residuals of an area-level regression have a significant positive Moran's I. What is the main consequence? - The regression coefficients become zero in each of the fitted models - The model must be refitted using fewer of the areas in the data - Standard errors are probably too small, so p-values are optimistic - The outcome variable is spatially random and so should be dropped ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkkzxo.4t4hkm" data-show="VGhlIG91dGNvbWUgaW4gYW4gYXJlYSBpbmZsdWVuY2VzIGl0cyBuZWlnaGJvdXJzJyBvdXRj b21lcyAoY29udGFnaW9uKQ==" data-explain="QSBsYWcgbW9kZWwgaW5jbHVkZXMgdGhlIG5laWdoYm91cnMnIG91dGNvbWVzIGFzIGEgcHJl ZGljdG9yIChzcGlsbG92ZXIpLiBTaGFyZWQgdW5tZWFzdXJlZCBmYWN0b3JzIGFyZSB0aGUg dHlwaWNhbCByZWFzb24gZm9yIGEgc3BhdGlhbCBlcnJvciBtb2RlbC4="} Which situation points to a spatial LAG model? - An unmeasured exposure affects blocks that lie next to each other - The outcome in an area influences its neighbours' outcomes (contagion) - The residuals are normally distributed with a constant variance throughout - The covariates are strongly correlated with each other and with the outcome ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkld6e.4t4w20" data-show="QSBzcGF0aWFsIGxhZyBtb2RlbCBpcyB0aGUgYmV0dGVyIGNhbmRpZGF0ZQ==" data-explain="V2hlbiBib3RoIHBsYWluIHRlc3RzIGFyZSBzaWduaWZpY2FudCwgdGhlIHJvYnVzdCB2ZXJz aW9ucyBoZWxwIGRlY2lkZS4gT25seSB0aGUgcm9idXN0IGxhZyB0ZXN0IHJlbWFpbmluZyBz aWduaWZpY2FudCBmYXZvdXJzIHRoZSBsYWcgbW9kZWwu"} Both plain LM tests are significant, but only the robust lag test is. What do you conclude? - A spatial error model is the better candidate - Neither model is needed, so ordinary regression is fine - A spatial lag model is the better candidate - The tests are contradictory, so they should be ignored ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tklqf4.4t5aje" data-show="QSBjaGFuZ2UgaW4gb25lIGFyZWEgYWxzbyBjaGFuZ2VzIGl0cyBuZWlnaGJvdXJzJyBvdXRj b21lcw==" data-explain="VGhyb3VnaCB0aGUgc3BhdGlhbCBtdWx0aXBsaWVyLCBhIGNoYW5nZSBpbiB4IGluIG9uZSBh cmVhIGNoYW5nZXMgeSB0aGVyZSBhbmQgaW4gbmVpZ2hib3VyaW5nIGFyZWFzLiBEaXJlY3Qs IGluZGlyZWN0IGFuZCB0b3RhbCBpbXBhY3RzIHJlcG9ydCB0aGVzZSBlZmZlY3RzLg=="} In a spatial lag model, why is the coefficient of a covariate not its full effect? - The coefficient is divided by the number of areas in the study - Lag models estimate the effects for the neighbours, not for the area - The coefficient is measured on a different scale from the outcome - A change in one area also changes its neighbours' outcomes ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="tkm3nq.4t5p0o" data-show="VGhlIHJlc2lkdWFsIE1vcmFuJ3MgSSwgd2hpY2ggc2hvdWxkIG5vdyBiZSBjbG9zZSB0byAw " data-explain="QSBzcGF0aWFsIG1vZGVsIGlzIG1lYW50IHRvIGFic29yYiB0aGUgc3BhdGlhbCBzdHJ1Y3R1 cmUuIElmIHJlc2lkdWFscyBzdGlsbCBzaG93IGF1dG9jb3JyZWxhdGlvbiwgdGhlIG1vZGVs IChvciB3ZWlnaHRzKSBuZWVkcyByZXRoaW5raW5nLg=="} After fitting a spatial error model, what should you check? - The residual Moran's I, which should now be close to 0 - Whether the number of blocks has doubled during fitting - That each covariate has become significant at the 5% level - Whether the lambda value has become equal to 1 ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Always test residuals** of an area-level regression (`lm.morantest`) - **LM tests** (and robust versions) suggest lag or error; theory should agree - Report **rho / lambda**, AIC vs OLS, the residual check; use **impacts** for lag - For counts with unequal populations, consider **Poisson models with spatial random effects** ::: **Next:** Back to the cheat sheet and the **Dungeons & Dataframes** GIS world (coming)

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
